data.why: The app ships 8 built-in example datasets (fetched from the gh-pages branch during install, served from app/examples/) and its own self-contained gzipped chemiscope JSON (docs/src/datasets/showcase.json.gz) that matches the Load Dataset file picker's expected .json.gz format.

goals: Browse a 2D/3D map of structural descriptors for a dataset of molecules or materials and spot clusters or outliers
Click a point on the map to inspect the corresponding 3D atomic structure and its computed properties side by side
Switch which properties drive the map's x, y, color and size axes to look for correlations between descriptors and physical properties
Play through a trajectory or series of structures (e.g. Azaphenacenes, Amorphous-Silicon) to see how structure and properties co-vary
Load a custom dataset (JSON or gzipped JSON) prepared with the chemiscope Python package and explore it the same way
Save the current visualization state (settings, selections) or the dataset itself back out as a JSON file to share or resume later

review.summary: The tree captures what chemiscope is for: linking a descriptor map to 3D structures and their properties, at the per-structure and per-atom level, then saving and sharing. The phases, wording and evidence are mostly sound. It needs small fixes before filing: three save/export nodes cite screens that don't show the result, f4's marker colour is wrong, the untested load-settings and 3D-click selection should be flagged, and f7 should be split, with an image-export feature added.
